current.text: Charlotte traded him to Minnesota. He is a starter there next to Anthony Edwards.
He is expected to run the Minnesota offense and to handle the ball much more than Edwards. Experts expect him to be the team's top assist man.
Experts expect his minutes to rise from 28 to about 30 to 32 a night. They expect his usage to fall to about 28%. More minutes should keep his assists steady or push them up.
Minnesota traded Julius Randle and Naz Reid and is very thin on size. It may start three guards. Ball has no other good passer beside him.
With Randle and Reid gone, he should pick up more rebounds and shots.
He looks good in preseason. Experts think he fits well with Edwards, and their three-point volume can coexist.

Experts rate him a mid second round player in categories, about top 20. That is a little above his Yahoo rank of 23. They call him a mild target at his price. In a mock auction he was valued in the mid 30s USD and bought for 30 USD.
The newest notes are not worried about his ankles this season. One expert says to drop him a tier if you expect only 28 minutes or about 50 games.
Minnesota has a two-game week starting March 15, inside our fantasy playoffs. With a March 28 end the playoff schedule is 4, 2, 4 games.
Because of the playoff two-game week, move him down slightly when two players are close.
Minnesota has the league minimum of 13 back-to-backs.
Minnesota should be competitive, so he should not be rested for tanking. One expert predicts 53 wins.

durable.text: He has a long history of ankle injuries, including impingement. He has played 70 or more games twice.
Experts disagree on his health risk. Some call it the biggest question about him. Others say the ankle fears are overblown because many of his missed games were tied to Charlotte tanking.
In Charlotte he ran about 30% usage with a high assist rate.
He is one of the best passers and transition players in the NBA, and an underrated offensive player.
He takes a very high share of his shots from three and has unlimited range. Threes and assists are his strongest categories, far above the pool.
Finishing at the rim is his biggest weakness. His FG% is low on high volume and hurts a team's FG%. He gets to the free throw line little.
He commits many turnovers, a clear weakness in the TO category.
He adds rebounds and steals that assist guards usually do not. He has posted seasons of 6 rebounds, 8 assists and 1.8 steals.

note: Experts value him in the mid 30s USD, a bit above his Yahoo value (32 USD) and the 29 USD he cost in our league last season. ESPN's 50 USD looks too high, so any price up to the mid 30s is fair. He fits best in punt FG% and punt TO builds, where his elite threes and assists come with no penalty and his FT%, steals and guard rebounds add value. Early in the season, check that his minutes reach about 32, that his assists hold next to Edwards, and how his ankles hold up. Expect a two-game week in our playoffs (week of March 15).
